done_when: From an item's second review round, review checks only the previous round's findings and the lines changed since that review; a new finding in unchanged code becomes a follow-up unless it is a security or data-loss problem; and a Not done finding blocks only against an owner-approved Done-when item, never a builder detail; in Forge's repo and in client repos, new and upgraded

known.title: Security findings identified by category can become nonblocking follow-ups
Not done: Deleting a line can make an unchanged finding block the next review
Gate: client guide proof does not check the Not done rule

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security — On a later review, a finding on an unchanged line with `category: security` becomes a follow-up if its body omits the exact `Raise: Security` text. `_finding` discards the structured category, and this check reads only the body; `score.holds` then makes the finding nonblocking. The new test covers only bodies that contain the Raise text.
findings.title: Security findings identified by category can become nonblocking follow-ups

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done — The approved Done-when requires new findings on unchanged code to become follow-ups from the second round. For a deletion-only hunk, Git reports a new-side count of zero. Coercing that count to one treats the preceding, unchanged line as changed. A worker who deletes a line to repair a finding can therefore face a new blocker cited on that unchanged line, restarting the review loop. The convergence test covers a replacement, not a deletion.
findings.follow_up: Not done names no owner-approved Done-when item; builder details are guidance.
findings.title: Not done: Deleting a line can make an unchanged finding block the next review

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test — The new and previously adopted client cases call `guides()`, but it asserts only the convergence sentence. Removing the new owner-approved `Not done` guidance from either shipped guide would leave these tests green, so the named proof does not establish that new and upgraded clients receive that part of the rule.
findings.title: Gate: client guide proof does not check the Not done rule

why: Close reviews take 4 to 9 rounds on code parts because every round reviews afresh and finds new edge cases, and builder details block as Not done
